stage1.impression: A dark, level shopfront at night with a big grey lightbox carrying a dancer's silhouette, a flat blue-grey EARF wordmark, and a warm, blurry room behind glass that shows no reflections. The street, the stall riser and the left-hand building fall into near-black, the Edwardian bay is cropped off, and the red speaker is a small pink smudge under the lettering. The surfaces are smooth and uniform and there is no sign of life, so it reads as a clean CG proof, not a night photograph.

blocking_9: Frame lum_median at 22 to 40 (now 12.1), with the pavement and stall riser holding detail instead of going to black
The Ember speaker readable at a glance as the frame's one saturated colour, not hidden under the window lettering and washed out to pink
The window wordmark reading as warm frosted or back-lit acrylic, not a flat blue-grey sign that competes with the speaker
The shopfront glass reflecting the street faintly (street lamps, the building opposite), so the glass reads as present
The building's Edwardian bay in frame, as the card's brief for the frame asks
Real material texture at 1:1 on the pavement, the blackened-steel frame and the building facade (the pour, the patina, wet or worn paving), and some sign of life

defects.what: Underexposed overall: lum_median 12.1, 78.9 % of pixels below 40
Stall riser below the glass is crushed (lum_median 1.2, crush_pct 84): a black slab with no steel texture
Pavement flat and dark (lum_median 9.4, crush 18 %), a uniform tiled plane with no wear, wet sheen or pools from the street lamps
Neighbouring facade almost black (crush 33 %), with a flat grey louvred panel at the left edge that reads as a placeholder
EARF wordmark is flat blue-grey (r 99, g 110, b 122), opaque and evenly lit: it reads as vinyl signage and is the strongest saturated colour in the frame, ahead of the speaker
The Ember speaker is a tiny, washed-out pink patch (r 201, g 147, b 131) half hidden behind the lettering, so it is not the hero
The lightbox is a cold neutral grey (130, 127, 130) against a warm room: it reads like a fluorescent panel, and the dancer silhouette has a hard clip-art look
The shopfront glass has no reflections at all, so it reads as an empty opening
Transom strip lights read as thin CG lines, and the facade above them (the bay) is cropped out
The room behind the glass is smeared by the denoiser or the depth of field: the shelves and the record wall are soft blobs with no edges

changes.problem: The frame is far too dark for a magazine night exterior, so the street, the riser and the facade drop to black.
changes.expected: Frame median about 25 to 32 with no clipping outside the lamps; the lightbox rises to about 150 to 170 (c6 brings it back down).

changes.problem: The street lamps barely reach the pavement or the shopfront, so the lower third of the frame is dead.

change.to: 260 W, 3400 K, one placed behind the camera at about 4 m high so that it grazes the pavement and the steel riser

changes.expected: Soft pools on the pavement falling off toward the frame edges; the riser's blackened steel shows a soft sheen and its edges; pavement median about 20 to 30.

changes.problem: The camera crops off the Edwardian bay the frame is meant to show, and its line of sight puts the window lettering over the Ember speaker.

evidence.measured: the speaker is about 30 x 24 px, under the wordmark, with the transom at the top edge and no bay visible

change.to: position [-9.0, 3.0, 1.6], level, 35 mm with a vertical lens shift of +0.18 so the bay's sill and the first floor are in frame and the verticals stay true; the target moved so the Ember pair sits in the clear glass to the right of the lettering

changes.expected: The bay fills the top quarter of the frame; the shopfront sits in the lower middle; the red speaker is seen through clear glass, not through the lettering.

changes.problem: The window's frosted name reads as flat blue-grey vinyl and is the frame's dominant colour, ahead of the speaker.

evidence.measured: r 99, g 110, b 122 median: cool and opaque against a warm 2400 to 2700 K room

change.setting: the window's frosted name emission and the frosted acrylic's roughness
change.to: emission 0.5 at 2700 K, frosted roughness raised so the room's light diffuses through it, with its polished edges catching the light

changes.expected: Warm off-white letters glowing softly with brighter edges; no blue cast; the speaker becomes the only saturated colour.

changes.problem: The shopfront glass reflects nothing, so it reads as an open hole rather than glazing.

evidence.measured: no reflected highlights from the street lamps anywhere in the glazing

change.from: effectively transparent with no visible reflection
change.to: clear float glass with a Fresnel reflection of about 4 to 8 % (IOR 1.52), so the street lamps and a dim facade across the street show faintly in the lower panes

changes.expected: A few soft reflected highlights and a faint ghost of the street in the riser-height glass; the room still reads clearly through it.

changes.problem: The lightbox is a cold grey slab that will blow out once exposure rises and that fights the warm room.

evidence.measured: lum_median 127.9, r 130, g 127, b 130: neutral against a room at r 64, g 43, b 29

change.to: 0.45 with a warmer white near 3200 K, and the frosted panel's roughness raised so the silhouette's edge softens further

changes.expected: After c1 the box sits about 135 to 155, slightly warm, glowing evenly; the dancer is a softer and more suggestive shadow.

changes.problem: The Ember speaker is washed to pink because the area lamps on it are too hot for its tint to read.

evidence.measured: lum_median 158, r 201, g 147, b 131: a low-saturation pink

change.setting: lamps: on each Ember speaker 2 x area
change.to: 18 W/m2, 2700 K, lowered and moved toward the back so that the light passes through the red acrylic instead of washing its face

changes.expected: A deeper, saturated red glow through the cabinet that reads as the frame's one colour; its region median about 90 to 130 with r well above g.

changes.problem: The frame has no atmosphere or sign of life, and the room behind the glass is smeared.

evidence.measured: the shelves and the record wall are soft blobs; the window ledge and the street are empty

change.from: haze 0.02, no props in the window, f/4.0 focused on the glass
change.to: haze 0.035; a couple of rocks glasses, a candle votive and a folded menu on the window ledge or a bar top seen through the glass; f/5.6 with focus 2 m inside the glass, so the room's edges hold

changes.expected: A faint glow in the room's air around the pendants, small highlights on the glasses, and readable shelf and record edges.

out_of_scope.request: Redraw the dancer silhouette so it is less clip-art (its odd head shape and hard edges)
out_of_scope.why: What the screens show is fixed by the card; only their brightness and the frosting may change (c6).

out_of_scope.request: Change the wordmark's letterforms or how it is mounted in the window
out_of_scope.why: The shopfront is part of the room's fixed design; only its light level and finish are adjusted (c4).

out_of_scope.request: Make the Ember speaker larger or more prominent in the room
out_of_scope.why: The speaker and its placement in the listening room are fixed; it can be served only by the camera (c3) and its lamps (c7).

out_of_scope.request: Add texture detail to the facade, the paving and the neighbouring louvred panel
out_of_scope.why: Partly an asset change to the street geometry, which the card does not list as changeable; the concrete's and the steel's finish can be roughened within c2 and c5.
